# Level code -> engine boundary (generated by tools/levels/boundary.py)

What the original level sections (kept as x86 from the player's dump) need from the engine: our own engine
implementation must keep every item here at the same address and layout (or a compatible thunk).

Level functions scanned: 5325 (PROLOGUE 673, ORAN 465, TUNISIA 313, KASSPASS 526, KASSRINE 250, LIBEATOR 327, GELA 417, PIANLUPO 411, TROINA 242, OMAHEACH 332, MONS1 542, EILEDORF 186, BUCHHOLZ 461, DRAGEETH 180).

| direct calls into .text | 391 functions | 50363 |
| calls into another level section | 162 functions | 8042 |
| shared globals (.data/.bss) | 47 | 107 |
| level-private globals (no contract) | 1561 | 24927 |
| block words past the slots | 31 | 5677 |
| struct fields via a global | 1045 | 10248 |

| level code addresses stored by level code (callbacks) | 1807 | |
| .rdata operands (dump data, no contract) | | 4696 |

## Runtime contract (not addresses)

- SEH: 3536 level functions link an exception frame through fs:[0] (fs:0x0 10735 sites); handlers end in the engine's MSVC
  ___CxxFrameHandler with the levels' own FuncInfo tables in .rdata. FS must point at an NT_TIB whose
  ExceptionList is per script thread (the thread switch must save/restore it), and C++ throws from
  level code must unwind through engine C frames correctly (or never cross them).
- MSVC CRT entry points called directly: _ftol, LIBCMT::_CxxThrowException, ??_M@YGXPAXIHP6EX0@Z@Z.
- Script threads: the Scr_Wait* family is called directly (call sites under 'Direct engine calls'); it
  switches the level code's native x86 stack, so our engine keeps stack-switching threads for level code.
- Calling conventions: each function's original one (seen: caller-cleaned pushes for slot calls,
  ecx = this for ScriptString_*; not checked per function yet - fnpack.py shows it).

## Shared script objects (pointers the levels publish in block words)

Each level's entry constructs objects (its own ctors and vtables), keeps the pointers in its .bss block
(prologue: 0x00921cbc..) and publishes them in block words past the slots; the engine's BroScr_* runtime
(compiled shared scripts in .text) and Scr_* read them there. Because the level code builds them, every
offset the engine uses is layout the engine must keep, and offsets on both sides doubly so; level-only
offsets are the level's own variables. Grouped by block words that always hold the same pointer.
